newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian military seizes poll boycott pamphlets.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian military seizes poll boycott pamphlets.

text.p: The military has seized at least 6,000 pamphlets asking Indonesians to boycott the May 29 general elections and is searching for those responsible for producing the material, Media Indonesia newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The newspaper quoted Major-General Tayo Tarmadi, head of the Siliwangi military command which oversees West Java province, as saying on Tuesday that the pamphlets had been found at a boarding house in Bandung, the capital of West Java.
"The content of the illegal pamphlets does not only discredit the New Order, but also ask people to boycott the general elections," Tarmadi was quoted as saying.
Military officials were not available for comment. The New Order is the term used to describe President Suharto's government after he rose to power in the mid 1960s.

Only three political parties are allowed to put up candidates for elections in Indonesia and some voters stay away from polling in protest. The government has banned any encouragements for people not to vote.

Tarmadi said the military was searching for a number of people suspected of producing the pamphlets and added about 200 of them had been distributed. He said the military believed the pamphlets would be distributed nationwide by the suspects.
The newspaper gave no other details.
